key_insight: Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT) transfers editing capabilities from an image editor to pretrained video editors without requiring new paired source-and-edited videos. It aims to improve existing editing skills and enable new editing tasks.
problem_solved: Video editing models lag behind image editors partly because paired source-and-edited videos are difficult to collect, limiting training data and task coverage.
method: Use an image editor to transfer editing capabilities to a pretrained video editor.
Post-train the video editor without collecting new paired video examples.
Improve existing editing capabilities and expand support to new editing tasks.
impact: I2VT offers practitioners a way to upgrade video editors while reducing reliance on costly paired-video datasets. The provided abstract is truncated, so implementation details and quantitative gains are not available.
visual_elements: Transfer diagram: image editor → I2VT post-training → upgraded video editor.
Data-requirement comparison: paired-video collection versus transfer without new paired videos.
Capability map distinguishing improved existing tasks from newly supported tasks.
Before-and-after video-frame storyboard illustrating an editing instruction; label it as conceptual.
paper_title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
paper_authors: Ji Xie, Yanhao Jia, Xiangpeng Yang, Martin Q. Ma, Sihan Xu
